name: Replica protocols seminar
scenario: One student uses the same course category for pencil traces, new safety arguments, and the final write-up. The requested part of the handout determines what counts as finished.

sections.heading: System
sections.body: A directory allocates exclusive leases for a key. An epoch change seals the old grant list on durable storage. Messages sent before the seal may arrive later.

sections.heading: A. Trace
sections.body: Draw a timeline with one delayed grant, two directory epochs, and one client retry. Annotate which epoch each participant records.

sections.heading: B. Argument
sections.body: Propose a condition a replica must check before admitting a client. Use induction over message delivery and crash recovery to justify it. State the durable state explicitly.

sections.heading: C. Optional
sections.body: Explain which change would be necessary if durable storage could be rolled back.

tasks.title: Typeset the lease solution
tasks.description: Turn the checked event order and proof outline into two clean pages. Label the figure and make the notation consistent.
tasks.details: All reasoning is in my notebook; no additional cases requested.

tasks.title: Check three acknowledgment histories
tasks.description: For each supplied message trace, mark whether an append has reached the stated replication threshold and underline the decisive event.
tasks.details: Only a mark and a one-line explanation are required.

tasks.title: Prove the snapshot cut is closed
tasks.description: Write a safety argument that includes buffered sends, duplicate barrier markers, and the first event at a recovering node.
tasks.details: I know the no-crash argument. The restart case is new to me.

tasks.title: Build a counterexample to the FIFO shortcut
tasks.description: Give the shortest sequence I can find that makes a receiver reveal a later message while its predecessor is still queued. Check all channel assumptions.
tasks.details: Need something concrete enough to present on the board.

holdouts.title: Solve part B of the bridge handout
holdouts.description: Prove the bridge never exposes a new route before every admitted old-route packet has been accounted for, or give a legal failure trace.
holdouts.details: Write the reasoning from scratch. Part A is already done.

pdf.title: Safe updates at a routing bridge

sections.heading: Setup
sections.body: A bridge tracks a configuration generation and a durable cutoff sequence number. Packets may be duplicated, delayed, and delivered after the controller restarts.

sections.heading: Part A. Replay
sections.body: Fill in missing generation labels for the sample execution in which a duplicate arrives after a cutoff. This part needs only the labels.

sections.heading: Part B. Safety
sections.body: Give an invariant for packets admitted before the cutoff. Cover controller recovery and a delayed acknowledgment in separate cases. If the listed fields are insufficient, construct an event sequence showing why.

sections.heading: Submission
sections.body: For B, give the state assumptions and either a proof or a numbered trace with the violated condition identified. A diagram without the argument is incomplete.

holdouts.check: Should favor the epoch and barrier arguments over quick trace-marking tasks in the same course.

holdouts.title: Check a bridge execution before section
holdouts.description: Work through the sample twenty-event log and circle the first transition that closes the old generation. Add one sentence explaining the choice.
holdouts.details: The proof is not due for this exercise; only the marked execution is requested.
holdouts.check: Shared terminology with a hard proof should not dominate a short replay exercise.
